title: Register to vote

Who can register to vote (1): If you live in England or Northern Ireland (6)
If you live in Scotland or Wales (2)

Register to vote: LEAD You can register to vote if you’re a British citizen or an Irish citizen.
If you live in England or Northern Irela: You must be aged 16 or over to register.
PRIZE You can register to vote if you’re a British citizen or an Irish citizen.
You can also register if you have permission (or do not need permission) to enter or stay in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man and you’re:
a Commonwealth citizen (including citizens of Cyprus and Malta)
a citizen of Denmark, Luxembourg, Poland, Portugal or Spain
a citizen of another EU country, who on or before 31 December 2020 had permission to enter or stay (or did not need permission) and this has continued without a break
If you live abroad: You can register as an overseas voter if you’ve previously lived in the UK and are either:
an eligible Irish citizen registering to vote in Northern Ireland
You’ll need to give the postcode of the last UK address you were registered to vote at.
If you’ve never registered to vote, you’ll need to give the postcode of the last UK address you lived at.
If you live in Scotland or Wales: You must be aged 14 or over to register.
You can also register if you have permission to enter or stay in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man, or you do not need permission.
Register using a paper form: You can register using a paper form in England, Wales and Scotland.
You’ll need to print, fill in and send the form to your electoral registration office.
After you’ve registered: Your name and address will appear on the electoral register.
It will also appear on the ‘open’ register unless you asked to opt out when registering.
Who can register to vote: You can register to vote up to 2 years before you reach voting age - check the rules around voting in the UK.
Get help registering: You can get help registering from your electoral registration office.
